annotations.title: Apply your classification rules to the whole IFC model

description:
Turn what you read in the overview into rules the tool replays on
EVERY piece of the model, including the ones you were never shown.

NOT NEEDED ON A MODEL ALREADY TREATED: when read_ifc_overview returns
'designation_existante', the units and fans are already designated -
reuse them. Posting rules REPLACES that designation entirely: do it
only when the user asks to start again, or when the designation
plainly contradicts what they say.

THIS IS HOW THE TOOL LEARNS A MODEL. read_ifc_overview gives you one
line per family of types, not one per piece. You answer with
RULES on those groups, and this tool applies them to the three thousand
pieces. You never give a verdict piece by piece: the result stays
deterministic because a program, not you, does the matching.

THEN READ THE ANSWER BACK, AND EXPECT TO POST AGAIN. The answer gives
every group with the role your rules gave it and how many pieces that
is. A rule that is too wide shows up on one line — « Gaine
rectangulaire cadree, 471 pieces, centrale_de_traitement_d_air » is a
rule that turned every duct into an air handling unit. Narrow it and
post again. Calling this tool costs nothing and may be repeated as
often as you need.

WHAT NEEDS A ROLE, AND WHAT DOES NOT. Plain ducts and fittings need
none: they are network by nature, and the answer marks them
segment_ou_raccord so you can see at a glance whether a rule caught
them by mistake. What needs a role is everything else — air handling
units, fans, fire dampers, balancing dampers, silencers, louvres,
diffusers — plus whatever must be kept OUT of the network, such as
access zones, equipment plinths or damper motors.

THREE ROLE NAMES ARE FIXED, because circuits start from them: give
air handling units, monoblocs and ventilation casings the role
centrale_de_traitement_d_air, fans the role ventilateur, and SMOKE
EXHAUST fans - including fans that bring compensation air for smoke
exhaust - the role ventilateur_desenfumage - exactly these words. A
smoke fan runs only in a fire, with the ventilation stopped: a duct
it shares with an air handling unit is not a plenum shared by two
installations, and the tool does not cut the networks there. Read
the names, families and types: « désenfumage », « DES », « smoke »,
« Entrauchung », « RWA ». ONLY EQUIPMENT THAT MOVES THE AIR gets one of them: a
unit is a box with a fan in it. Heating and cooling coils, heat
exchangers, filters, silencers, dampers, fire dampers, VAV boxes,
humidifiers are NOT units: the air runs through them, they are
pieces of the network. Give them another role (coil, silencer,
damper...) or none - never one of the unit roles. A coil in
'equipements' is a rule that is too wide. The answer lists, under
'equipements', the GUIDs of every piece of the model that got one of
these roles: that list is what trace_duct_circuits starts from,
and what the pages show as units. Every other role name is yours to
choose.

A MONOBLOC BUILT FROM MODULES. Many air handling units are modelled
as casings set end to end, each its own piece: filter casing, coil
casing, heat exchanger or heat recovery casing, humidifier, washer,
fan section, damper casing, empty casing. Give every such MODULE the
role composant_de_monobloc - exactly these words - and its fan
section(s) the unit role as usual. The tool then joins the modules
that touch each other face to face (over 0.25 m2 of contact) into ONE
unit: every duct on any module becomes one of its branches, and two
fans of the same casing become one unit. Only modules of a unit get
this role: a coil, a filter or a silencer fitted IN a duct is a piece
of the network, and an equipment frame or plinth is not a module.

ORDER THE LIST YOURSELF, most specific first, down to the most
general.
The fire damper rule must come before the balancing damper rule, or
« damper » takes everything. Equipment must come before terminals:
« VEN_MSF_MONOBLOC_SIMPLE_FLUX_REPRISE » contains « reprise », and a
return-diffuser rule placed first would claim the air handling unit.

Pieces no rule catches are simply listed, with no warning and no
failure: the engineer judges on the 3D view, not on a coverage report.

NEXT: once 'equipements' lists the air handling units and fans you
expect, call trace_duct_circuits with only the token. It computes
nothing yet: it checks that the units are connected to the networks
and returns the complete list of units and fans, to choose from -
see trace_duct_circuits. 'equipements' counts every piece
('pieces') but lists at most thirty names: the count, not the list,
is the model.
